verdict.rationale: Elicit's Chat/Compare feature explicitly lets analysts 'compare and contrast papers' and 'summarize multiple papers along specific dimensions,' and its column/table extraction lets you see each paper's data side-by-side, which supports spotting agreement/disagreement across sources. However, there is no dedicated feature that explicitly flags or highlights when sources conflict versus concur (no consensus/disagreement indicator), and community reports note the model can hallucinate quotes that contradict its own summaries, undermining confidence in cross-source synthesis. Missing for 10: an explicit contradiction/agreement-detection UI, and independent verification that comparisons are reliably accurate rather than hallucination-prone.
